q: 在限时的系统设计面试里，"模式"（patterns）的价值是什么？
options: 让方案听起来更学术，只是包装
套用验证过的最佳实践、提前预判常见故障点
可以替代对关键技术本身的理解
背熟模式名字就足以通过面试
options_en: It mostly makes your answer sound more academic.
You fall back on proven best practices and anticipate common failure modes ahead of time.
It can substitute for actually understanding the key technologies.
Memorizing pattern names alone is enough to pass the interview.
why: 识别模式能让你直接套用已验证的解法、提前预见常见故障模式，把现场发明轮子的时间省下来——这常是资深与初级工程师在系统设计面试里的分水岭。
why_en: Recognizing patterns lets you fall back on proven best practices and spot common failure modes ahead of time, which often separates senior from junior engineers.
q_en: In a time-boxed system design interview, what value do patterns provide?
optionExplanations: 把模式当包装话术站不住脚：面试官一深挖细节，你说不出具体故障点就露馅。
对：省去现场重新发明解法的力气，还能提前想到常见的坑，这才是分水岭所在。
模式代替不了对底层技术的理解，遇到变体设问照样答不上来。
光背模式名字扛不住追问，面试官会继续问为什么用、代价是什么。
optionExplanations_en: Treating patterns as packaging falls apart the moment the interviewer probes for a real failure mode.
Right: it saves you from reinventing a solution on the spot and gives you a head start on where things typically break.
Patterns cannot stand in for understanding the underlying technology, so any variant question breaks the illusion.
Naming a pattern alone will not survive a follow-up about why you picked it or what it costs.
scenario: 面试只有 35 分钟要设计一个直播弹幕系统，没时间从零推导每个组件的取舍。
scenario_en: You have 35 minutes to design a live-stream chat system, so there's no time to derive every component's tradeoffs from scratch.

q: 系统设计面试里这批常见模式（轮询/SSE、队列+worker、分片、CDN 直传）彼此是什么关系？
options: 互斥关系，一个系统只能选一种模式
不互斥，一个系统里经常同时组合好几个模式
有严格先后顺序，必须按顺序引入
每种模式绑定一家特定公司的技术栈
options_en: They are mutually exclusive; a system can only use one pattern.
They are not mutually exclusive; a real system usually combines several at once.
They must be applied in one strict, fixed order.
Each pattern is tied to one specific company's tech stack.
why: 模式不互斥：一个系统常常同时用到好几个，比如视频平台会同时用大文件、长任务、实时更新、多步流程等模式协同工作。
why_en: These patterns are not mutually exclusive, and a system like a video platform typically combines several of them at once.
q_en: How do common system design patterns relate to each other in an interview design?
optionExplanations: 把模式当单选题会误伤本该并存的方案，比如同时需要推送和后台处理时你只能选一个。
对：真实系统常常几个模式叠着用，选型看的是每个子问题各自的约束。
模式之间没有强制先后，只有迁移计划这类特殊场景才需要固定步骤。
模式是通用套路而不是某家公司专属，看到熟悉的公司名不该成为弃用理由。
optionExplanations_en: Treating patterns as a single choice forces you to drop one you actually still need, like push delivery alongside background processing.
Right: real systems usually stack several patterns at once, each answering a different subproblem's constraints.
There is no mandatory sequence between patterns; only an explicit migration plan needs a fixed order.
Patterns are general techniques, not one company's property, so recognizing a familiar name is not a reason to skip one.
scenario: 设计 YouTube：既有 GB 级上传和转码长任务，又要实时更新播放量，还要全球分发。
scenario_en: Designing YouTube: you have gigabyte uploads, long transcoding jobs, live view counts, and global delivery all in one system.

scenario: 设计一个需要向用户推送实时更新的功能，正在选协议，暂时没有证据表明简单方案撑不住。
q: 推荐的起点协议是？
options: 直接上 WebSocket，一步到位
先轮询，不够用再上 SSE/WebSocket
先用 SSE，因为看起来最省事
自研基于 TCP 的私有协议
options_en: Jump straight to WebSocket from day one.
Start with HTTP polling and upgrade to SSE or WebSocket once polling no longer serves your needs.
Start with SSE because it looks like the least work.
Build a custom protocol on raw TCP.
why: HTTP 轮询最简单虽不最高效；SSE 和 WebSocket 为实时而生，但基础设施更难做对。通用建议：从轮询开始，不够用了再升级。
why_en: Start with simple HTTP polling and only move to server-sent events or WebSocket once polling no longer serves your needs.
whenOtherWins: 当轮询的延迟或开销确实撑不住高频双向通信（如聊天、协同编辑）时，SSE 或 WebSocket 才登场。
tradeoff: 实现简单、轮询开销 vs 实时性更好、基础设施更复杂
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Poll["Polling"] --> SSE["SSE"]
    SSE --> WS["WebSocket"]
    Poll --> Simple["start simple"]

rows: 无证据证明简单方案不够用
只需服务器推给客户端
几乎不需要，运维成本极高

codeSample:
GET /messages?after=1719999000 HTTP/1.1
Host: chat.example.com

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"messages": [], "after": 1719999005}

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器单向推送协议：服务器通过一条 HTTP 长连接持续向客户端发事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events let a server push a stream of events to a client over one long-lived HTTP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种全双工长连接协议，客户端和服务器可以随时互相发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a full-duplex long-lived connection where client and server can send messages to each other at any time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流；HTTP、WebSocket 都构建在它之上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is the transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream, and both HTTP and WebSocket are built on top of it.

q_en: Which protocol should you start with?
scenario_en: You are designing a feature that pushes realtime updates to users. You are choosing a protocol, and there is no evidence yet that the simplest option cannot handle the load.
optionExplanations: 有明确证据要撑高频双向通信（如协同编辑）时才该直接上 WebSocket，本题还没验证需求就先背上连接管理的复杂度。
对：需求未验证时先用轮询这个最低运维成本的基线，等真扛不住延迟或吞吐再升级到 SSE/WebSocket。
SSE 适合已确定只需服务器单向推送的场景，本题只是图省事，还没验证轮询是否够用就跳过了它。
自研传输层协议只在现成协议全都不满足特殊约束时才值得，这里的运维成本远超收益。
optionExplanations_en: Jump to WebSocket only once you have evidence for high-frequency bidirectional traffic like collaborative editing; here the need is unproven and you would front-load connection-management cost.
Right: start with polling, the lowest-ops baseline, and upgrade once latency or throughput actually fails to keep up.
SSE fits once one-way server push is a confirmed requirement; here it just looks convenient and skips validating whether polling is already enough.
A custom transport protocol only pays off when every off-the-shelf option fails a real constraint; the ops cost here would dwarf the benefit.

q: 补全实时更新的三种协议选项：
text: 实时更新的协议选项：最简单的 HTTP {{轮询}}；专为实时而生的 {{SSE}}（服务器单向推送）和 {{WebSocket}}（双向长连接）——后两者的基础设施更难做对。
why: 同步 API 返回响应就够了；聊天、通知、实时看板需要推送。三个协议档位：轮询最简单、SSE 单向推送、WebSocket 双向长连接。
why_en: Realtime updates can use simple HTTP polling, one-way server-sent events, or two-way WebSocket, with the latter two trickier to operate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器单向推送协议：服务器通过一条 HTTP 长连接持续向客户端发事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events let a server push a stream of events to a client over one long-lived HTTP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种全双工长连接协议，客户端和服务器可以随时互相发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a full-duplex long-lived connection where client and server can send messages to each other at any time.

q_en: Fill in the three protocol options for realtime updates.

scenario: 类 WhatsApp 的聊天系统：服务端要把消息推给在线用户，希望把"发消息的服务"和"维持用户连接的服务"解耦。
q: 服务端常用的推送架构是？
options: Pub/Sub 服务解耦发布者和订阅者
所有用户连到同一台服务器
每条消息写库后靠客户端定时全量拉取
用 CDN 边缘节点推送消息
options_en: A Pub/Sub service decouples publishers from subscribers.
Connect every user to a single server.
Write each message to the database and let clients periodically pull everything.
Push messages through CDN edge nodes.
why: 服务端实时推送常用 Pub/Sub：发布者和订阅者解耦，WhatsApp 类聊天就用它；处理更重的场景（如 Google Docs）则用一致性哈希环组织有状态服务器。
why_en: Pub/Sub services decouple publishers from subscribers for realtime delivery, as in a WhatsApp-style chat system.
whenOtherWins: 当每个连接的处理本身很重（如 Google Docs 协同编辑），用一致性哈希环组织的有状态服务器更合适。
tradeoff: 发布订阅解耦 vs 有状态服务器承载更重的单会话处理

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布订阅模式：发布者把消息发给一个主题，订阅者从主题收消息，两者互不感知对方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Publish/Subscribe is a messaging pattern where publishers send to a topic and subscribers read from it, with neither side aware of the other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点，主要用于静态内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers close to users, mainly for static content.

q_en: What server-side push architecture is commonly used here?
scenario_en: In a WhatsApp-style chat system, the server must push messages to online users while keeping message producers decoupled from connection holders.
optionExplanations: 对：发布者不用关心谁在监听，订阅者上下线也不影响发布方，天然适合聊天这种多对多推送。
把所有用户接到一台服务器只在极小规模或本地原型能扛住，用户量一涨这台机器就是单点故障和容量天花板。
定时全量拉取延迟高、写库压力大，实时性要求越高这套方案越吃不消。
CDN 边缘节点是为可缓存的静态内容设计的，逐用户的实时消息路由不是它的强项。
optionExplanations_en: Right: publishers never need to know who is listening, and subscribers can connect or drop without touching the publish side, which fits many-to-many chat delivery.
Pinning every user to one server only survives tiny scale or a local prototype; growth turns that box into a single point of failure and a hard capacity ceiling.
Periodic full pulls add latency and heavy database write load, and the pain grows with how realtime the feature needs to be.
CDN edge nodes are built for cacheable static content, not per-user realtime message routing.

q: 实时推送的服务端方案：Pub/Sub 与"一致性哈希环上的有状态服务器"各自的优势是什么？
options: 两者完全等价，可以互换
Pub/Sub 适合重计算，哈希环适合轻转发
哈希环方案只能用来存数据库数据
Pub/Sub 胜在解耦；哈希环胜在扛住重会话
options_en: The two are fully equivalent and interchangeable.
Pub/Sub suits heavy computation while the hash ring suits light forwarding.
The hash ring approach can only be used to store database data.
Pub/Sub wins on decoupling publishers and subscribers; the hash ring wins on heavier per-session processing.
why: Pub/Sub 让发布方不关心谁在听、天然解耦；当会话本身有重处理（如 Google Docs 协同编辑），把状态固定到哈希环上的服务器更合适。
why_en: Pub/Sub wins on decoupling publishers from subscribers, while stateful servers on a consistent hash ring suit heavier per-session processing.
tradeoff: 解耦、易水平扩展 vs 承载更重的有状态单会话逻辑

rows: 状态固定在某台服务器

q_en: For realtime push, what are the strengths of Pub/Sub and stateful servers on a consistent hash ring?
optionExplanations: 两者管理状态的方式完全不同：Pub/Sub 无状态转发，哈希环把状态钉死在某台服务器，不能随意互换。
把负载类型配反了：真正吃重计算的是需要固定状态的会话（如协同编辑），Pub/Sub 更擅长轻量扇出。
哈希环的用途不止存数据库数据，它同样能把某类会话稳定路由到同一台有状态服务器。
对：轻量、无状态的扇出交给 Pub/Sub；需要在同一台服务器上持续维护会话状态的重处理交给哈希环。
optionExplanations_en: They manage state completely differently: Pub/Sub forwards statelessly while a hash ring pins state to one server, so they are not interchangeable.
This swaps the workloads: sessions that need pinned state, like collaborative editing, are the heavy case, while Pub/Sub is better at light fan-out.
Hash rings are not limited to storing database rows; they also route a given session consistently to the same stateful server.
Right: hand light, stateless fan-out to Pub/Sub, and hand heavier per-session work that must stay on one server to the hash ring.
scenario: 一个平台既要向全站广播通知，又要支撑 Google Docs 式每个文档会话都带重状态的协同编辑。
scenario_en: One platform has to broadcast site-wide notifications and also run Google-Docs-style collaborative editing where each document session carries heavy state.

q: 什么样的功能才需要"推送实时更新"这个模式？
options: 所有 API 都需要
只有游戏类应用需要
聊天、通知、实时看板：事件发生要立即触达用户
只要系统整体采用了微服务架构就需要
options_en: Every API needs it.
Only games need it.
Chat, notifications, and live dashboards, where users must be reached the instant an event happens.
Any system that has broadly adopted a microservices architecture needs it.
why: 同步 API 完成请求后返回响应就够了；只有聊天、通知、实时看板这类"事件发生就要让用户看到"的场景才需要推送式实时更新。
why_en: Synchronous APIs simply return a response, while chat, notifications, and live dashboards need updates pushed the moment they happen.
q_en: What kind of feature actually needs the realtime-push pattern?
optionExplanations: 把推送当成默认需求会给同步请求-响应接口加上不必要的连接管理成本。
游戏只是众多例子之一，不是划界的标准，会漏掉聊天、看板这些同样需要推送的场景。
对：判断标准是事件发生后用户是否必须立刻看到，聊天、通知、看板都属于这一类。
微服务只决定服务怎么拆分，不决定要不要推送，两者是不同维度的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Treating push as a default adds needless connection-management cost to endpoints that only need request-response.
Games are just one example, not the actual boundary, so this misses chat and dashboards that need push just as much.
Right: the test is whether a user must see an event the instant it happens, which covers chat, notifications, and dashboards.
Microservices only decide how services are split; they say nothing about whether push is needed.
scenario: 电商后台：订单详情查询走同步 API 就够，但库存告警要在事件发生后秒级触达运营。
scenario_en: In an e-commerce back office, order lookups are fine over a plain synchronous API, but stock alerts have to reach operators within seconds of the event.

scenario: 用户提交视频转码、报表生成、批量操作等耗时远超几秒的任务，不能让请求同步等待。
q: "管理长任务"模式的核心做法是？
options: 把 HTTP 请求超时调成 10 分钟
立即确认+后台处理：入队后秒级返回 job ID
让客户端保持连接直到任务完成
把任务全部放进数据库触发器里跑
options_en: Just extend the HTTP request timeout to ten minutes.
Split it into immediate acknowledgment plus background processing: enqueue after validation and return a job ID in milliseconds while workers execute it.
Keep the client connection open until the task finishes.
Run the entire task inside a database trigger.
why: 长任务模式 = 即时确认 + 后台处理：Web 服务器校验请求、把作业推进队列，毫秒级返回 job ID；独立的 worker 池从队列拉活执行。
why_en: Split long operations into immediate acknowledgment and background processing: enqueue a job, return a job ID in milliseconds, and let workers execute it.
whenOtherWins: 作业本来就短时别急着塞队列：同步返回结果架构更简单、背压更清晰、用户体验更好。
tradeoff: 响应快、可独立扩缩 vs 多一层队列和状态跟踪的运维复杂度
codeSample:
LPUSH jobs:transcode '{"jobId":"abc123","videoUrl":"s3://in/1.mp4"}'
# Web 服务器校验完立刻入队，毫秒级把 jobId 返回给用户

BRPOP jobs:transcode 0
# worker 阻塞式拉取到作业后异步执行真正的转码

termDefinitions.meaning: 作业提交后系统返回的唯一标识，用于后续查询任务状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A job ID is the unique identifier returned after submission, used to check the task's status later.

q_en: What is the core move in the long-running-task pattern?
scenario_en: Users submit work such as video transcoding, report generation, or bulk operations. Each job takes far longer than a few seconds, so the request must not wait synchronously.
optionExplanations: 调大超时只能扛住几十秒级的延迟，分钟级的转码或报表任务照样会撞上新的上限。
对：请求校验完立刻入队、毫秒级返回 job ID，真正的执行交给独立 worker 池，响应快且两层能各自扩缩。
长连接只适合等待时间短、并发量低的场景，分钟级任务会占满连接池、拖垮并发能力。
数据库触发器适合小数据量的约束检查，塞进耗时业务逻辑既难调试也无法独立扩容。
optionExplanations_en: A longer timeout only buys you tens of seconds; a minute-long transcode or report job will hit a new ceiling anyway.
Right: validate and enqueue immediately, return the job ID in milliseconds, and let a separate worker pool do the real work, so both layers scale independently.
Holding the connection open only fits short waits with low concurrency; a minute-long job will exhaust the connection pool.
Database triggers fit small constraint checks; stuffing long business logic into one is hard to debug and cannot scale on its own.

q: 把长任务处理的流程排成正确顺序：
steps: worker 持续从队列拉取作业并执行真正的工作
用户提交一个耗时任务
毫秒级返回 job ID 给用户
Web 服务器立即校验请求，把作业推入队列（Redis / Kafka）
why: 提交 → 校验并入队 → 立刻返回 job ID → worker 异步执行。好处：用户响应快、Web 与 worker 独立扩缩、故障隔离。
why_en: The user submits a task, the server validates and enqueues it, returns a job ID instantly, and workers pull and execute it in the background.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    U["用户提交任务"] --> W["Web服务器：校验"]
    W --> Q["队列 (Redis/Kafka)"]
    W --> R["毫秒级返回 job ID"]
    Q --> K["worker池拉取执行"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，这里可当轻量消息队列用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store, used here as a lightweight message queue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息队列/流处理平台，适合高吞吐的作业分发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming and message-queue platform suited to high-throughput job distribution.

q_en: Put the long-running-task flow in the correct order.

q: "队列 + worker 池"的长任务架构带来哪三个好处？
options: 响应快、独立扩缩、故障隔离
零延迟、零成本、零运维
不再需要重试机制
所有任务都能强一致
options_en: Fast user responses, independent scaling of web servers and workers, and fault isolation.
Zero latency, zero cost, and zero operations.
You no longer need a retry mechanism.
Every task becomes strongly consistent.
why: 把重活挪到队列后面：请求毫秒级返回；Web 层和 worker 池按各自负载扩缩；worker 挂了不影响接请求，三者互相隔离。
why_en: Queue-plus-workers gives fast user responses, independent scaling of web servers and workers, and fault isolation.
q_en: What three benefits does a queue-plus-worker architecture provide for long-running tasks?
optionExplanations: 对：响应交给入队环节，Web 层和 worker 各自按负载扩缩，一方故障不牵连另一方。
队列本身要部署、监控、扩容，运维和延迟成本都真实存在，不存在零成本这回事。
异步反而更需要重试和幂等兜底，消息丢失、重复投递都要业务自己处理。
队列不自带强一致性，跨服务的原子性还是要靠事务或协调协议。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the response returns as soon as the job is enqueued, web tier and workers scale to their own load, and a worker crash does not take down the request path.
A queue still needs deployment, monitoring, and scaling, so real ops and latency cost exists; nothing about it is free.
Async work needs retries and idempotency even more, since duplicate or lost messages become the caller's problem.
A queue does not grant strong consistency on its own; cross-service atomicity still needs transactions or coordination.
scenario: 视频平台上传后要转码 10 分钟，HTTP 请求不能挂这么久，于是改成队列 + worker 池。
scenario_en: On a video platform transcoding takes ten minutes, far too long to hold an HTTP request open, so the work moves behind a queue and a worker pool.

q: 候选人一上来就把处理逻辑塞到队列后面，为什么这经常是坏决定？
options: 队列的软件许可成本太高
作业短的话，同步返回更简单、体验更好
队列天生不支持重试
worker 进程无法水平扩展
options_en: Message queue software licensing is too expensive.
If the job is already short, returning the result synchronously keeps the architecture simpler with clearer backpressure and better user experience.
Queues inherently do not support retries.
Worker processes cannot scale horizontally.
why: 异步化不是免费的：短作业同步返回状态，架构大幅简化、背压天然清晰、用户立刻拿到结果。只有真正的长任务才值得队列+worker的复杂度。
why_en: For short-running jobs, returning the result synchronously keeps the architecture dramatically simpler with clearer backpressure and better user experience.
q_en: Why is putting work behind a queue from the start often a bad call?
optionExplanations: 许可成本从来不是这里讨论的重点，多数队列方案本身开销不在授权费上。
对：作业本来就短的话，同步返回让架构简单、背压清楚，用户立刻拿到结果，没必要为此多加一层队列。
多数消息队列原生就支持重试，这个说法本身就是错的。
worker 池正是为了水平扩展后台执行力而存在的，这个说法把它的用途说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Licensing cost is not the issue being discussed here; most queue setups are not gated by license fees.
Right: if the job is already short, a synchronous response keeps the architecture simple, backpressure obvious, and the user gets the result immediately, so a queue adds cost with no payoff.
This is simply false; most message queues natively support retries.
This reverses the point; worker pools exist specifically to scale background execution horizontally.
scenario: 一个接口只做 200ms 的缩略图裁剪，候选人却先把它塞到队列后面异步化。
scenario_en: An endpoint only does a 200-millisecond thumbnail crop, yet the candidate immediately pushes it behind a queue to make it asynchronous.

q: 落地长任务模式时，除了队列和 worker 池，还必须处理哪些配套问题？
options: 前端的像素级还原
DNS 解析优化
数据库范式化
状态跟踪、重试、死信队列兜底
options_en: Pixel-perfect frontend rendering.
DNS resolution optimization.
Database normalization.
Job status tracking, retries, and a dead letter queue for messages that keep failing.
why: 核心技术是消息队列（作业协调）+ worker 池（执行）；配套必须有作业状态跟踪、重试，以及死信队列处理反复失败的毒消息。
why_en: Beyond queues and worker pools you must handle job status tracking, retries, and dead letter queues for poison messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门收纳反复处理失败的消息的队列，避免"毒消息"无限重试拖垮系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead letter queue collects messages that repeatedly fail processing, so poison messages do not retry forever and drag down the system.

q_en: Besides queues and worker pools, what companion mechanisms must long-running tasks handle?
optionExplanations: 前端展示精度和作业能否可靠完成是两件事，跟长任务落地无关。
DNS 解析优化针对的是域名查找瓶颈，帮不上作业生命周期管理。
数据库范式化解决的是数据建模问题，不处理失败作业怎么被发现和兜底。
对：失败作业要能被追踪、重试，反复失败的毒消息要有死信队列收纳，否则它们会拖垮整条队列。
optionExplanations_en: Frontend pixel accuracy and whether a job completes reliably are unrelated concerns.
DNS tuning targets domain-lookup bottlenecks, not how a background job status gets tracked and cleaned up.
Database normalization is a data-modeling concern; it says nothing about catching or handling failed jobs.
Right: failed jobs need tracking and retries, and messages that keep failing need a dead letter queue so they do not clog the pipeline forever.
scenario: 视频转码流水线上线后，某些坏文件让 worker 反复 OOM，同一条消息被无限重投。
scenario_en: After the transcoding pipeline ships, a few corrupt files make workers run out of memory repeatedly and the same message gets redelivered forever.

scenario: 多个用户同时抢最后一张演唱会门票，或同时对同一拍卖品出价——同一资源被并发访问。
q: 这类问题的本质与该套用的模式是？
options: 读扩展问题，加只读副本
竞争问题：需要防竞态、保一致的协调机制
大文件问题，用预签名 URL
实时更新问题，加 WebSocket
options_en: A read-scaling problem, so add read replicas.
A contention problem that needs coordination mechanisms like locks or transactions to prevent race conditions.
A large-blob problem, so use a presigned URL.
A realtime-update problem, so add WebSocket.
why: 多方同时访问同一资源就是竞争模式的领域：要用锁、事务等机制防止竞态条件、保证数据一致，这是分布式系统的协调难题。
why_en: Multiple users grabbing the same ticket is a contention problem that needs coordination mechanisms to prevent race conditions.
whenOtherWins: 如果并发访问的是不同资源、没有共享写目标，就没有竞争问题，普通的扩展手段即可。
tradeoff: 强一致的协调开销 vs 允许竞态导致超卖

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个操作并发访问同一份数据、结果取决于执行顺序而产生的不一致 bug。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is a bug where concurrent operations on the same data produce inconsistent results depending on execution order.

q_en: What is the nature of this problem, and which pattern should you apply?
scenario_en: Multiple users are grabbing the last concert ticket or bidding on the same auction item at the same time, so one shared resource is being accessed concurrently.
optionExplanations: 加只读副本只在读容量不够时管用，这里的问题是同一张票被两个事务同时改，副本救不了。
对：多个请求要写同一份库存，得靠锁或事务把并发写串起来，才能保证不超卖。
预签名 URL 解决的是大文件字节怎么绕开服务器，跟同一资源的并发写冲突无关。
WebSocket 只负责把结果推给客户端，推送快慢不能保证库存数字本身是对的。
optionExplanations_en: Read replicas only help when read capacity is short; here the problem is two transactions racing to change the same ticket count, which replicas cannot fix.
Right: multiple requests are writing the same inventory row, so you need a lock or transaction to serialize the writes and prevent overselling.
Presigned URLs solve how large file bytes bypass the server; they have nothing to do with concurrent writes to one resource.
WebSocket only pushes results to clients faster; push speed cannot guarantee the inventory number itself is correct.

q: 处理竞争（contention）的手段谱系包括哪些？（多选）
options: 数据库层：悲观锁、乐观并发控制（OCC）
分布式协调：分布式锁、两阶段提交（2PC）
基于队列的串行化
给客户端加载入动画掩盖延迟
options_en: Database-level: pessimistic locking and optimistic concurrency control.
Distributed coordination: distributed locks and two-phase commit.
Queue-based serialization.
Adding a loading animation on the client to mask latency.
why: 方案从数据库级（悲观锁、OCC）到分布式协调（分布式锁、2PC、队列串行化）。关键是分清什么时候用事务/原子性、什么时候用显式锁。
why_en: Contention solutions range from pessimistic locking and optimistic concurrency control to distributed locks, two-phase commit, and queue-based serialization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 乐观并发控制：先假设不会冲突、写时校验版本号，冲突了再重试，而不是提前加锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare, checks a version number at write time, and retries on conflict instead of locking upfront.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两阶段提交：协调者先让所有参与者"准备好"，都同意了再统一"提交"，用于跨库/跨服务的原子性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-Phase Commit has a coordinator ask every participant to prepare, then commits only once all agree, giving atomicity across databases or services.

q_en: Which techniques belong in the contention-handling toolbox? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 挡住单库内的竞态：悲观锁先占住行阻塞别人，OCC 先假设不冲突、写时校验版本号再重试。
挡住跨服务/跨库的不一致：分布式锁协调共享资源，2PC 让所有参与者先准备好再统一提交。
挡住乱序执行：把并发请求排进一条队列逐个处理，用牺牲并发度换来严格顺序。
只是掩盖了用户感知到的延迟，数据本身该冲突还是会冲突，什么都没挡住。
optionExplanations_en: Blocks contention inside one database: pessimistic locking holds a row so others wait, while OCC assumes no conflict and checks a version at write time before retrying.
Blocks inconsistency across services or databases: distributed locks coordinate a shared resource, and two-phase commit waits for every participant to prepare before committing.
Blocks out-of-order execution: it funnels concurrent requests through one queue and trades concurrency for strict ordering.
This only hides latency the user perceives; the underlying data can still race and corrupt exactly as before.
scenario: 演唱会开票瞬间，同一个座位被上千个请求同时争抢，不能超卖。
scenario_en: The moment concert tickets drop, thousands of requests fight over the same seat and you cannot oversell it.

q: 解决竞争问题时，推荐的演进顺序是？
options: 一开始就上分布式锁和 2PC 显得更专业
先用队列串行化，再考虑数据库方案
先单库方案解决，规模到了再上分布式协调
永远不要用数据库锁
options_en: Start with distributed locks and two-phase commit to look more sophisticated.
Start with queue-based serialization, then consider the database.
Start with single-database solutions like transactions and locks, upgrading to distributed coordination only when scale demands it.
Never use database locks at all.
why: 大多数问题先用单数据库方案起步（事务与锁足够），确有规模需求再引入分布式协调。权衡是性能与一致性保证、简单方案与复杂协调之间的取舍。
why_en: Most contention problems start with single-database solutions and only scale to distributed coordination when necessary.
q_en: What is the recommended evolution path for solving contention?
optionExplanations: 一上来就上分布式锁和 2PC 是在为还不存在的规模买单，单库机制往往就够用。
顺序反了：队列串行化是为特定资源准备的重手段，不该抢在数据库方案之前。
对：先让数据库自带的事务和锁解决问题，规模真撑不住了再引入分布式协调。
数据库锁是解决单库竞争最基础的工具，只有锁冲突代价真的无法接受时才该绕开它。
optionExplanations_en: Reaching for distributed locks and two-phase commit up front pays a coordination cost for scale you do not have yet; single-database tools are usually enough.
This gets the order backwards; queue-based serialization is a heavier tool for specific resources and should not come before the database solution.
Right: let the database's own transactions and locks solve it first, and only bring in distributed coordination once scale genuinely demands it.
Database locks are the most basic tool for single-database contention; skip them only when lock-contention cost is truly unacceptable.
scenario: 日订单十万级的票务系统存在座位争抢，但单库 Postgres 的 CPU 还只用了三成。
scenario_en: A ticketing system with a hundred thousand orders a day has seat contention, but its single Postgres instance is still only about thirty percent utilized.

q: 把数据过早拆分到多个数据库，会带来什么后果？
options: 把数据库原本替你解决的竞争难题全部揽到了自己身上
性能一定提升，没有任何代价
数据会自动跨库保持一致
只会影响备份和恢复的速度，不影响一致性
options_en: You take on all the contention problems the database was designed to solve for you.
Performance always improves with no downside.
Data automatically stays consistent across databases.
It only affects backup and recovery speed, not consistency.
why: 数据库本身就是围绕竞争问题设计的；一旦拆库，事务、锁等保障就没了，这些难题都归你。拆分有时合理，但别过早——面试官会深挖你是否理解代价。
why_en: Splitting data across databases means taking on all the contention problems databases were designed to solve, so avoid doing it prematurely.
q_en: What happens if you split data across multiple databases too early?
optionExplanations: 对：单库时事务和锁替你兜住的竞争问题，拆库后全部变成应用自己要重新解决的难题。
拆库常常引入跨库事务和锁的新开销，性能不会无条件变好。
跨库一致性恰恰是拆分后最难的部分，不会自动保持。
拆库影响的不只是备份，事务边界和锁的保障范围也跟着变了。
optionExplanations_en: Right: transactions and locks that a single database handled for you become problems the application must reimplement after a split.
Splitting often adds cross-database transaction and locking overhead, so performance does not improve unconditionally.
Cross-database consistency is exactly the hardest part after a split; it does not stay consistent on its own.
A split changes more than backups; transaction boundaries and locking guarantees shift too.
scenario: 订单量仍在单库能扛的范围，有人提议先按用户 ID 拆成 8 个独立数据库。
scenario_en: Order volume still fits comfortably in one database, but someone proposes splitting it into eight separate databases by user ID right now.

scenario: 评估一个典型 Web 应用（如图片社交 App）该往读路径还是写路径投入优化预算。
q: 典型应用的读写比大约是多少，这对架构投入意味着什么？
options: 1:1，读写投入应该对半开
起步约 10:1，常达 100:1 以上
写远多于读，应优先优化写路径
2:1 封顶，读写优化力度接近
options_en: About one to one, so split effort evenly between reads and writes.
Starting around ten to one and often exceeding one hundred to one, so optimizing the read path pays off far more than the write path.
Writes far outnumber reads, so prioritize the write path.
It caps around two to one, so give reads and writes similar effort.
why: 读写比 = 每次写触发的读次数，通常从 10:1 起步、往往到 100:1 以上。想想 Instagram：刷几十张照片要几百次查询，你一天可能只发一帖；这个比例决定了要优先投入读路径（索引、副本、缓存），而不是写路径。
why_en: Read-to-write ratios start around ten to one and often exceed one hundred to one, as in Instagram, which tells you to prioritize the read path first.
q_en: What read-to-write ratio is typical, and what does it imply for architecture investment?
scenario_en: You are deciding whether a typical web app, such as a photo-sharing product, should spend optimization effort on the read path or the write path.
optionExplanations: 1:1 的假设会让你把索引、缓存这些读优化预算平均分给写路径，白白浪费在不是瓶颈的地方。
对：读天然比写多一个数量级起步，图片类产品刷屏的查询量远超发帖次数，这决定了预算先给读路径。
把写当成大头会让你先去分片扩写，而多数 C 端应用第一个撞墙的其实是读。
把比例封顶在 2:1 会低估读的量级，实际到规模后索引和副本承受的压力远不止这个数。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming one to one would spread your indexing and caching budget evenly onto the write path, wasting it where the bottleneck is not.
Right: reads naturally outnumber writes by at least an order of magnitude — scrolling a photo feed fires far more queries than posting does — so budget goes to the read path first.
Treating writes as the bigger load pushes you toward sharding writes first, when most consumer apps actually hit the read wall first.
Capping the ratio at two to one understates real read volume; at scale, indexes and replicas absorb far more pressure than that.

q: 把"扩展读"的自然演进顺序排出来：
steps: 水平扩展：加只读副本（read replica）
先在数据库内部优化读性能：索引、反范式化
why: 扩展读的三级演进：库内优化（索引、反范式化）→ 只读副本 → 外部缓存（Redis/CDN）。从最便宜、最简单的手段开始逐级加码。
why_en: Scale reads by first optimizing within the database with indexes and denormalization, then adding read replicas, then external caches like Redis and CDNs.
tradeoff: 库内优化成本最低但收益有限 vs 外部缓存收益大但多一层运维和失效复杂度
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["1. 库内优化：索引/反范式化"] --> B["2. 只读副本"]
    B --> C["3. 外部缓存：Redis/CDN"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库的只读副本，通过复制同步主库数据，承接读流量以分担主库压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of the database, kept in sync via replication, that offloads read traffic from the primary.

q_en: Put the natural read-scaling evolution in order.

scenario: 应用从几百用户涨到百万用户，读流量成了第一个瓶颈，你要给出第一步应对措施。
q: 最该先做的是？
options: 立刻把数据库拆分成多个分片来扩容
重写成微服务
全站上 CDN
先在现有数据库内优化：加索引、做反范式化
options_en: Shard the database into multiple pieces for scale right away.
Rewrite everything as microservices.
Put the entire site behind a CDN.
Optimize inside the existing database first: add indexes and denormalize.
why: 读扩展从库内优化开始：索引和反范式化最便宜、见效快，然后才是只读副本和外部缓存。分片是写扩展的大招，别为读瓶颈先掏出来。
why_en: Start scaling reads by optimizing inside the database with indexing and denormalization before replicas or external caches.
whenOtherWins: 库内优化和副本都到位后仍扛不住，或有全球静态内容分发需求时，Redis 缓存与 CDN 才是下一步。
tradeoff: 改动小、见效快 vs 需要引入新组件和运维复杂度

rows: 读优化和副本都已用尽
团队/部署边界成为瓶颈
内容可缓存且用户地理分散
第一步，改动最小见效最快

q_en: What should you do first?
scenario_en: An application grows from hundreds of users to millions, read traffic becomes the first bottleneck, and you need to propose the first response.
optionExplanations: 分片适合数据量或写吞吐已经超过单库边界，这里读优化和副本都还没用上，成本明显超前。
重写微服务解决的是团队协作和部署边界问题，要花几个月，扛不住眼前的读压力。
CDN 缓存的是静态内容，个性化的动态查询它缓存不了，帮不上这波读瓶颈。
对：先加索引、做反范式化，这是改动最小、见效最快的一步，之后才轮到副本和外部缓存。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding fits once data size or write throughput exceeds one database's limits; here read optimization and replicas have not even been tried yet, so it is premature.
A microservices rewrite fixes team and deployment boundaries, and takes months, so it does nothing for read pressure today.
CDNs cache static content; they cannot cache personalized dynamic queries, so they do not touch this read bottleneck.
Right: add indexes and denormalize first — the smallest change with the fastest payoff — before reaching for replicas or an external cache.

q: 扩展读的三大关键难点是哪些？（多选）
options: 缓存失效（invalidation）的管理
只读副本的复制延迟（replication lag）
热 key：数百万用户同时请求同一热门内容
磁盘碎片整理
options_en: Managing cache invalidation.
Replication lag on read replicas.
Hot keys, where millions of users request the same popular content at once.
Disk defragmentation.
why: 读扩展的三大坑：缓存何时失效才不读到旧数据、副本延迟导致读到落后数据、热 key 把单节点打爆。这三个都是面试深挖点。
why_en: The key read-scaling considerations are cache invalidation, replication lag on read replicas, and hot keys for popular content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被远超其他 key 的并发请求集中访问的单个缓存/数据库键，容易压垮持有它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single cache or database key hit by disproportionately more concurrent requests than others, which can overwhelm the node holding it.

q_en: What are the three key challenges in scaling reads? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 挡不住就会读到过期数据：必须定义缓存什么时候失效、谁来触发失效。
挡不住就会读到落后写入的数据：副本从主库同步总有延迟，要接受或主动处理这个滞后。
挡不住就会打垮单个节点：热门内容被海量并发集中访问同一个 key，这个节点会先扛不住。
现代云存储的碎片整理通常是托管服务自己处理的，不是读扩展要操心的层面。
optionExplanations_en: Leave this unhandled and reads return stale data: you must define when the cache invalidates and who triggers it.
Leave this unhandled and reads fall behind writes: replication from primary to replica always lags, so you must accept or actively manage that gap.
Leave this unhandled and one node gets crushed: massive concurrent traffic concentrates on a single popular key faster than anything else fails.
Modern managed storage handles defragmentation itself; it is not a layer read-scaling design needs to worry about.
scenario: 新闻门户首页读写比约 1000:1，一条头条可能被上百万用户在同一分钟打开。
scenario_en: A news portal home page has a read-to-write ratio around a thousand to one, and one headline can be opened by millions of users within the same minute.

scenario: 写入量从每秒几百涨到每秒上百万，单台数据库服务器和存储系统撞上硬上限。
q: "扩展写"模式的核心策略是？
options: 分片+垂直分区+队列/丢弃应对突发
加更多只读副本
把所有写操作都改成异步日志
换更大配置的单机
options_en: Horizontal sharding across servers, plus vertical partitioning by data type, plus queues or load shedding for bursts.
Add more read replicas.
Turn every write operation into an asynchronous log entry.
Move to a bigger single machine.
why: 写扩展三板斧：水平分片摊数据、垂直分区按数据类型拆、队列缓冲/负载丢弃应对突发。副本解决的是读，不是写。
why_en: Scaling writes relies on horizontal sharding, vertical partitioning, and handling bursts with queues and load shedding.
whenOtherWins: 如果瓶颈其实是读而不是写，只读副本和缓存就够了，别急着分片。
tradeoff: 分摊写压力、可持续扩展 vs 引入跨分片查询和路由复杂度
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Writes["Write bottleneck"] --> Shard["Horizontal sharding"]
    Writes --> Vertical["Vertical partition"]
    Burst["Bursty writes"] --> Queue["Queue / shed load"]
q_en: What is the core strategy for scaling writes?
scenario_en: Write traffic grows from hundreds per second to millions per second, and a single database or storage server hits a hard ceiling.
optionExplanations: 对：水平分片把数据摊开、垂直分区按类型隔离、队列或丢弃扛住突发，三个手段各管一段写压力。
只读副本承接的是读流量，主库本身的写入目标数量一个没变，帮不了写瓶颈。
写成异步日志只是把落盘时机往后挪，最终字节还是要落到同一批有限的存储上。
垂直扩容有明确的硬件天花板，撞上之后就再没有单纯加配置这条路了。
optionExplanations_en: Right: horizontal sharding spreads the data, vertical partitioning isolates data by type, and queues or shedding absorb bursts — three tools for three slices of write pressure.
Read replicas absorb read traffic; the number of write targets on the primary never changes, so this does nothing for a write bottleneck.
Turning writes into an async log just delays when bytes land; they still end up on the same finite storage in the end.
Vertical scaling has a hard hardware ceiling, and once you hit it there is no more 'just add resources' left to do.

q: 好的分区键（partition key）要同时满足哪两个条件？
options: 全局唯一且自增
尽量短且是整数
负载摊匀到各分片，相关数据留同片
按时间顺序排序且保持不可变
options_en: Globally unique and auto-incrementing.
As short as possible and an integer.
Spread load evenly across shards while keeping related data on the same shard.
Sorted in time order and kept immutable.
why: 选分区键的两难：负载要均匀分布（避免热点分片），相关数据又要聚在一起（避免跨分片查询）。两者兼顾才是好键。
why_en: A good partition key distributes load evenly across shards while keeping related data together.
q_en: What two properties should a good partition key satisfy?
optionExplanations: 自增键保证唯一和递增，但新写入总落在最后一个分片，反而制造出热点。
短整数类型省存储空间，但和负载是否均匀分布完全是两回事。
对：既要让写入均匀摊开避免热点分片，又要让相关数据落在同一片避免跨片查询，两头都顾到才是好键。
按时间排序对范围查询友好，但高并发写入会挤在同一个时间段，同样会造热点。
optionExplanations_en: An auto-increment key guarantees uniqueness and ordering, but every new write lands on the last shard, which creates a hot spot.
A short integer type saves storage space, but that has nothing to do with whether load spreads evenly.
Right: spread writes evenly to avoid a hot shard while keeping related rows on the same shard to avoid cross-shard joins — a good key does both.
Sorting by time helps range queries, but high-concurrency writes then pile into the same time window and create the same kind of hot spot.
scenario: 给聊天应用的消息表分片：既有几万人的超级大群，又常按会话 ID 拉整段历史。
scenario_en: You are sharding a chat app’s message table: some rooms have tens of thousands of members, and reads usually pull a whole history by conversation ID.

scenario: 系统平时写入正常，但偶发短时写入洪峰远超容量；过载时希望优先保住重要的写入。
q: 两种应对突发写入的手段是？
options: 全部拒绝或全部接收，二选一
写队列缓冲尖峰；过载时负载丢弃保关键写
加只读副本
把写入改成每天一次批处理
options_en: Either reject everything or accept everything, pick one.
Buffer temporary spikes with a write queue, and use load shedding to prioritize important writes during overload.
Add read replicas.
Batch all writes once a day.
why: 临时尖峰用写队列缓冲；持续过载时用负载丢弃，牺牲低优先级写入保住关键写入。批处理可作为额外手段合并多个写、降低单次开销。
why_en: Buffer temporary spikes with write queues and use load shedding to prioritize important writes during overload.
whenOtherWins: 若洪峰是常态而非偶发，说明容量规划不足，该扩分片而不是永远靠队列硬扛。
tradeoff: 保住关键写入的可用性 vs 主动丢弃部分低优先级写入

termDefinitions.meaning: 负载丢弃：系统过载时主动拒绝或降级部分低优先级请求，保住核心功能可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load shedding is deliberately rejecting or degrading lower-priority requests during overload so the system's core functions stay available.

q_en: What are two ways to handle bursty writes?
scenario_en: The system usually handles writes fine, but occasional short write spikes exceed capacity. During overload, important writes should survive first.
optionExplanations: 非黑即白只适合灾难开关：全部接收会压垮系统，全部拒绝又会误伤本该成功的正常写入。
对：短时尖峰先进队列缓冲住，扛不住的持续过载再丢弃低优先级写入，保住关键写入不丢。
只读副本承接的是读请求，对写入洪峰完全无能为力。
改成每天批处理会牺牲写入的实时可见性，对要求即时生效的写入并不适用。
optionExplanations_en: All-or-nothing fits an emergency kill switch: accepting everything crashes the system, rejecting everything hurts writes that should have gone through.
Right: buffer a short spike in a queue, and once overload is sustained, shed lower-priority writes to keep the critical ones alive.
Read replicas absorb read traffic; they do nothing for a burst of incoming writes.
Batching once a day sacrifices real-time visibility, which does not work for writes that need to take effect immediately.

q: 补全扩展写的策略清单：
text: 扩展写的策略：{{水平分片}}把数据摊到多台服务器；{{垂直分区}}把不同类型的数据分开存；写突发用{{队列}}缓冲或负载丢弃；{{批处理}}把多个写合并以摊薄单次操作开销。
why: 四件套覆盖了写瓶颈的不同侧面：分片摊流量、垂直分区隔离负载、队列/丢弃抗突发、批处理省开销。
why_en: Write scaling combines horizontal sharding, vertical partitioning, queue buffering or load shedding for bursts, and batching to reduce per-operation overhead.
q_en: Fill in the write-scaling strategy list.

scenario: 系统要收发视频等 GB 级大文件，不希望这些字节流经应用服务器把它拖成瓶颈。
q: "处理大文件"模式的做法是？
options: 应用服务器代理转发所有上传和下载请求
把文件切碎存进数据库表
预签名 URL：客户端直传 S3，CDN 下载
用 FTP 服务器中转
options_en: Have the application server proxy and relay every upload and download request.
Chop the file into pieces and store it in database tables.
Let clients talk to storage directly: the app server only issues a presigned URL for direct upload to S3, and downloads go through a CDN with a signed URL.
Relay everything through an FTP server.
why: 别让 GB 级数据穿过应用服务器：服务器只生成临时、限定范围的预签名 URL，客户端直传 S3；下载由 CDN 配签名 URL 提供。服务器不再是瓶颈，还顺带获得断点续传、进度跟踪和全球分发。
why_en: Generate presigned URLs so clients upload directly to blob storage and download from CDNs, keeping large files off your application servers.
whenOtherWins: 小文件（如头像缩略图）直接经服务器上传也无妨，不必为它引入预签名流程的复杂度。
tradeoff: 文件字节绕过服务器、可扩展 vs 元数据与存储状态需要额外同步机制
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client"] --> API["Get signed URL"]
    API --> DB["Metadata"]
    Client --> Blob["Upload to blob"]
    Blob --> CDN["Download via CDN"]

rows: GB 级视频、图片等大文件

codeSample:
POST /videos/upload-url            # 应用服务器签发
→ {"uploadUrl":"https://s3.../v.mp4?X-Amz-Signature=...","expiresIn":900}

PUT <uploadUrl>                     # 客户端直传，不经过应用服务器
Content-Type: video/mp4
<binary bytes>

termDefinitions.meaning: 带有效期和权限范围的临时授权链接，允许客户端直接对存储服务读写而无需暴露长期密钥。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presigned URL is a time-limited, scoped authorization link that lets a client read or write storage directly without exposing long-lived credentials.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，常用于存放图片、视频等大文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is AWS's object storage service, commonly used to hold large files like images and video.

q_en: What is the large-blob pattern?
scenario_en: The system must upload and download gigabyte-scale files such as videos, and those bytes should not flow through application servers.
optionExplanations: 应用代理适合小文件、低流量场景，GB 级字节全部穿服务器只会把它拖成瓶颈。
数据库不是为大二进制设计的，把视频切碎存进表里会让库迅速膨胀变慢。
对：服务器只签发限时授权的预签名 URL，字节直接在客户端和存储之间走，服务器负载和文件大小脱钩。
FTP 中转缺少断点续传、进度跟踪这些现代对象存储自带的能力，只适合遗留系统过渡。
optionExplanations_en: App proxying fits small, low-traffic files; routing gigabyte-scale bytes through the server turns it into the bottleneck.
Databases are not built for large binaries; chopping video into table rows bloats and slows the database fast.
Right: the server only issues a time-limited presigned URL, bytes flow directly between client and storage, and server load stops scaling with file size.
FTP relaying lacks resumable uploads and progress tracking that modern object storage gives you for free; it only fits legacy transition periods.

q: 大文件模式（客户端直传 + CDN 下载）的关键挑战是什么？如何缓解？
options: 元数据与存储状态同步，靠事件通知对齐
预签名 URL 永远不会过期
CDN 从架构上无法支持大文件
客户端从架构上无法直连 S3
options_en: Keeping database metadata in sync with blob storage and handling upload failures, mitigated by storage event notifications.
Presigned URLs never expire.
CDNs are architecturally unable to support large files.
Clients are architecturally unable to connect directly to S3.
why: 文件本体绕过了服务器，数据库里的元数据就可能与存储脱节：要处理上传失败、生命周期管理，并靠存储服务的事件通知把应用状态拉齐。
why_en: The key challenges are keeping database metadata in sync with blob storage and handling upload failures, mitigated by storage event notifications.
q_en: What is the key challenge in the large-blob pattern, and how do you mitigate it?
optionExplanations: 对：字节走的是另一条路，数据库这边保存的记录容易和存储里的真实情况脱钩，需要靠事件通知去对齐。
预签名 URL 应该短期有效，长期不过期反而会留下访问控制漏洞。
CDN 恰恰是给大文件下载做全球分发用的，这个说法是反的。
客户端直连对象存储正是这套模式的核心动作，说它连不上是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Right: bytes bypass the server, so database metadata can drift from actual storage state, and you need event notifications to reconcile the two.
Presigned URLs should be short-lived; staying valid forever would leave an access-control hole instead of fixing anything.
CDNs exist precisely to distribute large-file downloads globally, so this claim is backwards.
Direct client-to-storage connection is the core move of this pattern, so claiming it cannot connect is wrong.
scenario: 网盘单文件可达 5GB，客户端拿预签名 URL 直传 S3，数据库只留元数据。
scenario_en: In a file-storage product single files reach five gigabytes, so clients upload straight to S3 with a presigned URL and the database only keeps metadata.

scenario: 订单履约流程横跨多个服务、耗时长，必须扛得住失败、重试和外部依赖抖动，还要保证不重复执行。
q: 现代的推荐方案是？
options: 每个服务都自己存一份状态、手工写错误处理逻辑
用工作流引擎（如 Temporal）自动管理状态和重试
用 cron 每分钟检查一遍所有订单
把整个流程塞进一个数据库事务
options_en: Each service stores its own copy of state and hand-writes its own error-handling logic.
Use a workflow engine like Temporal or AWS Step Functions to automatically manage state, failure recovery, and retries.
Use a cron job that checks every order once a minute.
Squeeze the entire flow into a single database transaction.
why: 从状态散落各处、手工错误处理，转向声明式工作流：系统持久化状态、自动恢复和重试，并保留完整审计轨迹。外部 activity 仍可能重试，端到端效果要靠幂等或补偿才能接近 exactly-once。
why_en: Workflow engines like Temporal manage durable state, recovery, and retries automatically, though activities still need idempotency for exactly-once-like effects.
whenOtherWins: 流程简单、只在单服务内时，简单的单机编排就够了；事件溯源则是让每步发事件触发下一步的分布式替代方案。
tradeoff: 自动状态管理和审计 vs 引入工作流引擎的学习和运维成本
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Step1["Step 1"] --> WF["Workflow engine"]
    WF --> Step2["Step 2"]
    WF --> Retry["Retry / state"]
    WF --> Audit["Audit trail"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源的持久化工作流引擎，负责持久化每一步状态并自动处理失败重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal is an open-source durable workflow engine that persists each step's state and automatically handles failure retries.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的托管工作流服务，用状态机声明式地编排多个 Lambda/服务调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AWS Step Functions is a managed workflow service that orchestrates multiple Lambda or service calls declaratively as a state machine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，效果和只执行一次相同；分布式重试必须靠它避免重复副作用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating the same operation multiple times has the same effect as doing it once, which is essential for safe retries in distributed systems.

q_en: What is the modern recommended approach?
scenario_en: An order-fulfillment flow spans multiple services, runs for a long time, and must survive failures, retries, and flaky external dependencies without duplicate effects.
optionExplanations: 手写状态适合短流程、失败率低的场景，外部依赖一抖动，各服务各自为政就容易状态不一致。
对：把状态、重试、恢复都交给引擎持久化管理，还自带完整执行历史，比手写错误处理靠谱得多。
cron 轮询发现卡住的订单可能要等上快一分钟，精度和实时性都不够。
跨服务的操作本来就装不进一个数据库事务，这条路在技术上走不通。
optionExplanations_en: Hand-rolled state fits short, low-failure flows; the moment an external dependency wobbles, each service going its own way invites inconsistency.
Right: let the engine durably persist state, retries, and recovery, with a full execution history built in — far more reliable than hand-written error handling.
A cron poll might take almost a minute to notice a stuck order, which is neither precise nor timely enough.
A cross-service operation simply does not fit inside one database transaction; this path is not technically possible.

q: 事件溯源如何实现多步流程的分布式协调？
options: 每一步轮询数据库检查前一步是否完成
由一台中心服务器同步调用每一步
每一步完成时发出事件，事件触发后续步骤
所有步骤并行执行后再投票决定顺序
options_en: Each step polls the database to check whether the previous step finished.
One central server synchronously calls every step.
Each step emits an event when it finishes, and that event triggers the next step.
All steps run in parallel and then vote on the order afterward.
why: 事件溯源提供了分布式的编排方式：每个步骤发出事件，事件再触发下一步——没有中心协调者，链条自然向前推进。
why_en: With event sourcing each step emits events that trigger the subsequent steps, coordinating the workflow in a distributed way.
q_en: How does event sourcing coordinate a multi-step process in a distributed way?
optionExplanations: 轮询要不断查数据库确认上一步是否完成，引入延迟还加重数据库负担。
中心节点同步调用每一步会让这台服务器变成单点瓶颈，跟去中心化的初衷相反。
对：每步完成就发一个事件，事件本身触发下一步，链条不需要中心协调者也能往前走。
先并行跑完再投票决定顺序，把步骤间的依赖关系搞反了，谁先谁后本该由因果决定。
optionExplanations_en: Polling repeatedly queries the database to check the previous step, which adds latency and extra database load.
Having one central node synchronously call every step turns that server into a single-point bottleneck, the opposite of decentralization.
Right: each step fires an event when it finishes, and that event alone triggers the next step, so the chain moves forward without a central coordinator.
Running everything in parallel and voting afterward inverts the dependency; which step goes first should be decided by causality, not a vote.
scenario: 电商下单要走扣库存、支付、发货三个独立服务，团队不想引入中心协调者。
scenario_en: Placing an order spans three independent services for inventory, payment, and shipping, and the team does not want a central coordinator.

q: 补全多步流程模式的关键洞见：
text: 从散落的状态管理和手工错误处理，转向{{声明式}}的工作流定义：系统持久化状态和重试，业务侧通过{{幂等}}让 effect 接近 exactly-once，并维护完整的{{审计}}轨迹。
why: 这是多步流程模式的精髓：把状态、重试、恢复从业务代码里抽走，交给工作流系统统一管理；外部副作用仍要靠幂等、事务或补偿保证业务效果。订单履约、用户注册、支付处理都是典型场景。
why_en: The key insight is moving to declarative workflows where the system manages durable state and retries, while idempotent activities keep the effect exactly-once-like.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一操作重复执行多次，效果和只执行一次相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotency means repeating an operation multiple times has the same effect as doing it once.

q_en: Fill in the key insight of the multi-step-process pattern.

scenario: 设计 Uber 或 Gopuff：要按地理位置搜索附近的司机/仓库，实体数量在几十万到上百万。
q: 关键的技术选型是？
options: 全表扫描算每个实体的距离
按名称建普通 B-Tree 索引
把坐标当成普通字符串存储，再用 LIKE 做模糊匹配查询
地理空间索引（PostGIS/Redis/ES geo）
options_en: Full table scan computing distance for every entity.
A regular B-Tree index built on name.
Store coordinates as plain strings and match them later with a LIKE fuzzy query.
A geospatial index such as PostgreSQL with PostGIS, Redis geospatial types, or Elasticsearch geo-queries.
why: 按位置检索靠地理空间索引：常用商品数据库的扩展（PostGIS、Redis geospatial）或专用方案（Elasticsearch geo-queries）。思路是把地理区域切成可管理的小区、在区内建索引，快速排除大片无关区域。
why_en: Proximity search relies on geospatial indexes such as PostGIS, Redis geospatial types, or Elasticsearch geo-queries.
whenOtherWins: 只有约 1000 个实体时，直接全量扫描更划算——专用索引或服务的开销反而不值。
tradeoff: 查询速度随规模稳定 vs 引入专用索引/服务的额外运维成本
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Geo["Geo query"] --> Cells["Partition into cells"]
    Cells --> Nearby["Search nearby cells"]
    Nearby --> Rank["Filter by distance"]

rows: 无法按距离排序，效率差

codeSample:
SELECT id, name
FROM stores
WHERE ST_DWithin(
  location::geography,
  ST_MakePoint(-122.42, 37.77)::geography,
  2000              -- 搜索半径 2000 米
)
ORDER BY location <-> ST_MakePoint(-122.42, 37.77)
LIMIT 20;

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 的地理空间扩展，为数据库加上地理坐标类型和空间查询能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostGIS is a geospatial extension for PostgreSQL that adds geographic coordinate types and spatial query capabilities.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式搜索引擎，支持全文检索和地理位置（geo）查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a distributed search engine that supports full-text search as well as geo-location queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系数据库最常见的索引结构，适合一维有序数据的等值和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-Tree is the most common relational-database index structure, suited to equality and range queries over one-dimensional ordered data.

q_en: What is the key technology choice?
scenario_en: You are designing Uber or Gopuff-style nearby-driver or nearby-warehouse search, with hundreds of thousands to millions of entities.
optionExplanations: 全表算距离在十万级以上实体时延迟会线性变差，规模一大就扛不住。
B-Tree 是为一维有序数据设计的，理解不了经纬度这种二维距离关系。
把坐标存成字符串用 LIKE 匹配，既排不了序也过滤不出真正的邻近关系。
对：用地理空间索引把区域切成小格、区内建索引，查询时先裁掉大片无关区域，十万到百万级实体都扛得住。
optionExplanations_en: Full-scan distance math degrades linearly past roughly a hundred thousand entities and cannot keep up at scale.
B-Trees are built for one-dimensional ordered data; they cannot represent the two-dimensional distance relationship between coordinates.
Storing coordinates as strings and matching with LIKE can neither sort by distance nor filter for real proximity.
Right: a geospatial index cuts the map into cells and indexes within them, pruning vast irrelevant regions before comparing distance, which scales to hundreds of thousands or millions of entities.

q: 地理空间索引加速查询的基本思路是？
options: 划分成小区、区内索引，快速排除无关区域
把所有坐标缓存在内存里做暴力比较
给每个用户预计算到所有实体的距离
按邮编字母顺序排序
options_en: Divide the area into manageable regions and index entities within them, quickly excluding vast irrelevant areas.
Cache all coordinates in memory and brute-force compare them.
Precompute every user's distance to every entity.
Sort entities alphabetically by postal code.
why: 架构核心是分区 + 区内索引：查询时先排除大片无关区域，搜索空间骤减。这也是 geohash、四叉树等方案的共同思想。
why_en: Geospatial indexes divide the area into regions and index entities within them, letting queries quickly exclude vast irrelevant areas.
q_en: What is the basic idea behind speeding up queries with a geospatial index?
optionExplanations: 对：先把地图切成小区、区内建索引，查询时先裁掉无关的大片区域，搜索空间一下子小很多。
把所有坐标缓存进内存做暴力比较，比较开销随实体数线性增长，规模一大就撑不住。
给每个用户预算到所有实体的距离，用户和实体一多，这张表的规模会直接爆炸。
邮编顺序和物理距离不是一回事，相邻的邮编可能隔着很远。
optionExplanations_en: Right: cut the map into cells and index within them, so a query prunes vast irrelevant areas first and the search space shrinks fast.
Caching every coordinate in memory for brute-force comparison scales linearly with entity count and buckles as the dataset grows.
Precomputing every user's distance to every entity explodes in size as both populations grow.
Postal-code order and physical distance are not the same thing; neighboring codes can sit far apart.
scenario: 打车派单要在千万级司机位置里，50ms 内找出乘客 2 公里内的车。
scenario_en: A ride-hailing dispatcher must find cars within two kilometers of a rider in under fifty milliseconds, across tens of millions of driver positions.

scenario: 决定是否要为一个按位置搜索的功能引入专门的地理空间索引，而不是直接扫描全部实体。
q: 实体数量到什么量级，专门的地理空间索引才开始划算？
options: 只要超过 10 个实体就必须上专用索引
上千个就必须上专用索引
几十万到百万级才划算；约 1000 条全扫更简单
任何规模都必须上专用索引
options_en: You must add a dedicated index as soon as you pass ten entities.
You must add a dedicated index once you pass a thousand entities.
It pays off at hundreds of thousands to millions of entities; around a thousand, a full scan is simpler and cheaper.
You must always use a dedicated index at any scale.
why: 门槛在规模：约 1000 条时全表扫描 O(n) 距离计算本身够快，专用索引的部署运维开销不划算；几十万到百万级时，索引才能把候选实体从全量降到附近几个区，这个量级是决定要不要引入专用索引的基准。
why_en: Geospatial indexes only pay off at hundreds of thousands or millions of items; with about a thousand items a full scan is better and simpler.
q_en: At what scale does a dedicated geospatial index start to pay off?
scenario_en: You are deciding whether a location-search feature needs a dedicated geospatial index instead of scanning all entities.
optionExplanations: 十条左右上专用索引纯属过度设计，全表扫描的开销比部署一个地理索引服务低得多。
千级规模全表扫描本身已经够快，这时候引入专用索引换来的是运维成本而非收益。
对：几十万到百万级时全表扫描才真正线性变慢，这个规模区间专用索引换来的收益才盖过它的运维成本。
不看规模一律上专用索引，等于把一个千条数据的原型也背上不必要的运维负担。
optionExplanations_en: Indexing at around ten entities is pure over-engineering; a full scan costs far less than standing up a geospatial index service.
At roughly a thousand entities a full scan is already fast enough, so adding a dedicated index buys ops cost, not a real win.
Right: full scans only start degrading badly at hundreds of thousands to millions of entities, and that is the range where a dedicated index finally pays for its own upkeep.
Indexing regardless of scale saddles even a thousand-row prototype with operational overhead it never needed.

q: 关于邻近查询的地理范围，多数系统的实际情况是？
options: 用户经常做全球范围的邻近搜索
邻近查询通常找"本地"实体，很少全球查询
邻近查询必须支持跨洲检索
查询范围大小对索引设计没有影响
options_en: Users frequently run global-scale proximity searches.
Proximity queries usually mean the user is looking for entities local to them, rarely global.
Proximity queries must support cross-continent lookups.
Query range has no effect on index design.
why: 涉及邻近时，用户找的几乎都是身边的东西——这个观察能显著简化设计（如按城市/区域分片），不必为全球查询过度设计。
why_en: Most proximity systems serve users looking for entities local to them, not global queries.
q_en: For proximity queries, what geographic scope do most systems actually serve?
optionExplanations: 全球查询才是罕见情况，为它设计主路径会让大多数用户走一条被过度设计的路。
对：用户找的几乎都是身边的东西，这条观察让你可以按城市/区域分片，省下全球设计的复杂度。
跨洲检索只是极少数后台运营需求，不该成为主查询路径的设计前提。
查询范围恰恰是决定分片粒度和索引策略的关键约束，说它没影响是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Global-scale queries are the rare case; designing the main path around them over-engineers the experience for most users.
Right: users searching nearby are almost always looking for something close by, which lets you shard by city or region and skip the complexity of global design.
Cross-continent lookup is a rare admin or ops need, not something the main query path should be designed around.
Query scope is exactly the constraint that sets shard granularity and index strategy; claiming it has no effect is wrong.
scenario: 外卖 App 的"附近餐馆"查询里，99% 的请求半径不超过 5 公里。
scenario_en: In a food-delivery app’s nearby-restaurants query, ninety-nine percent of requests use a radius of five kilometers or less.

scenario: 设计一个视频平台：用户上传视频、平台转码、处理中要给用户看进度、上传-转码-发布要串成一条流程。
q: 这套需求会组合用到哪些模式？（多选）
options: 大文件模式：处理视频上传
长任务模式：视频转码
实时更新模式：推送处理进度通知
多步流程模式：编排整个上传-转码-发布工作流
options_en: Large blobs, for handling the video upload.
Long-running tasks, for transcoding.
Realtime updates, for pushing progress notifications.
Multi-step processes, to coordinate the entire upload-transcode-publish workflow.
why: 这正是"模式不互斥"的示范：视频平台同时用大文件（上传）、长任务（转码）、实时更新（进度）、多步流程（整体编排）四个模式协同工作。
why_en: A video platform combines large blobs for uploads, long-running tasks for transcoding, realtime updates for progress, and multi-step processes to coordinate the workflow.
tradeoff: 四个模式各自解决一个子问题、覆盖需求完整 vs 同时维护四套机制的架构复杂度
q_en: Which patterns does this video-platform requirement combine? (Select all that apply.)
scenario_en: You are designing a video platform: users upload videos, the platform transcodes them, users need progress updates, and upload-transcode-publish must be one flow.
optionExplanations: 挡住服务器被拖成瓶颈：GB 级视频字节靠预签名 URL 直传对象存储，不占应用服务器带宽。
挡住请求被转码耗时拖死：上传后立刻入队，交给独立 worker 池异步转码。
挡住用户干等看不到进展：转码状态变化时主动推给客户端，而不是让用户反复刷新。
挡住跨步骤失败后状态失控：上传-转码-发布串成一条工作流，失败重试和进度都有统一记录。
optionExplanations_en: Blocks the server from becoming the bottleneck: gigabyte-scale video bytes go straight to object storage via a presigned URL, never touching app-server bandwidth.
Blocks the request from being stuck on transcoding: the upload gets enqueued immediately and a separate worker pool transcodes it asynchronously.
Blocks users from staring at a stalled screen: progress changes get pushed to the client instead of making users refresh repeatedly.
Blocks state from spiraling out of control across steps: upload-transcode-publish is one workflow, with retries and progress tracked in one place.

q: 选择模式时的总原则是？
options: 一开始就用最复杂的架构方案来展示实力
先简单起步（轮询/单机编排），按需求加复杂度
每道题固定用全部模式
看面试官的表情反应决定
options_en: Open with the most complex architecture solution to show off skill.
Start with simpler approaches like polling and single-server orchestration, adding complexity only when specific requirements demand it.
Always apply every pattern regardless of the problem.
Decide based on the interviewer's facial expression.
why: 先简后繁：轮询先于 WebSocket、单机编排先于工作流引擎。识别哪些模式适用、理解其权衡，有具体需求再加复杂度——这展示的是架构成熟度。
why_en: Start with simpler approaches like polling and single-server orchestration, adding complexity only when specific requirements demand it.
q_en: What is the general rule for choosing patterns?
optionExplanations: 开局就上最复杂方案是在为还不存在的需求买单，容易被面试官问到答不出取舍。
对：先给轮询、单机编排这类最简单能跑的方案，等具体约束逼出来了再加复杂度。
不做取舍、每题都堆满全部模式，反而暴露的是判断力不足而不是全面。
面试官表情能帮你判断沟通效果，但不能替代真实的技术约束来做设计决策。
optionExplanations_en: Opening with the most complex solution pays a complexity tax for a need that is not established yet, and invites a trade-off question you cannot answer.
Right: start with the simplest thing that works, like polling or single-server orchestration, and add complexity once a real constraint forces it.
Stacking every pattern regardless of need signals weak judgment, not thoroughness.
An interviewer's expression can tell you how communication is landing, but it cannot replace an actual technical constraint as a design driver.
scenario: 45 分钟面试里设计一个通知系统，需求只写了"几秒内送达"，没有更强的实时约束。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute interview you design a notification system whose only stated requirement is delivery within a few seconds, nothing stricter.

q: 在面试中主动识别并套用这些模式，传达出什么信号？
options: 背题痕迹重，是减分项
说明候选人只懂抽象理论，完全不会落地实现
展示架构成熟度，并让你把时间花在设计中最重要的部分
对评分没有实质影响
options_en: It looks memorized and counts against you.
It means the candidate only understands abstract theory and cannot actually implement it.
It demonstrates architectural maturity and lets you focus time on the most important parts of the design.
It has no real effect on the score.
why: 主动识别模式 = 架构成熟度的信号；它还帮你聚焦设计里真正重要的部分，避免在实现细节里越陷越深。
why_en: Proactively identifying patterns demonstrates architectural maturity and keeps you focused on the most important parts of the design.
q_en: What signal do you send by proactively recognizing and applying these patterns in an interview?
optionExplanations: 死记硬背模式名字确实会减分，但能讲清楚为什么用、代价是什么，那是另一回事。
只点名模式而讲不出接口、状态、故障处理，才会显得脱离实践，这不是识别模式本身的问题。
对：主动点出模式说明你能把问题归类，还能把时间省下来花在真正的取舍点上。
评分确实会看你是否能抽象问题、复用成熟方案，这项能力不是无关紧要的。
optionExplanations_en: Rote-memorized names do cost you points, but explaining why you chose it and what it costs is a different skill entirely.
Naming a pattern without reaching interfaces, state, or failure handling is what looks impractical — that is not a flaw in recognizing patterns itself.
Right: naming the pattern up front shows you can categorize the problem, freeing your time for the trade-offs that actually matter.
Evaluation does weigh whether you can abstract a problem and reuse a proven solution; this skill is not beside the point.
scenario: 面试官抛出"设计 Dropbox"，你立刻认出这是大文件直传加多步流程两个模式的组合。
scenario_en: The interviewer says "design Dropbox," and you immediately recognize it as the large-blob upload pattern combined with a multi-step process.
